test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the correct pair from the following options.

options.text: Motion of a freely falling body - Non-uniform acceleration
Change in velocity per unit time - Acceleration
Velocity does not change with time - Non-uniform motion
Velocity varies with time - Uniform motion

solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in velocity per unit time - Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **2) Change in velocity per unit time - Acceleration:**
 
• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• This means that acceleration measures how quickly the velocity of an object is changing.
 
• It is a vector quantity, possessing both magnitude and direction.
 
• The units of acceleration are meters per second squared (m/s²).
 
• If the velocity increases, the acceleration is positive; if the velocity decreases, the acceleration is negative (deceleration or retardation).
 
• An object that speeds up, or slows down, or changes direction, is accelerating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) Motion of a freely falling body - Non-uniform acceleration:**
 
• A freely falling body experiences uniform acceleration due to gravity.
 
• The acceleration due to gravity is approximately 9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface, and it is considered constant.
 
• Therefore, the motion of a freely falling body is an example of uniform acceleration, not non-uniform acceleration.
 
• Air resistance can change the acceleration, but in a vacuum, the acceleration is constant.
 
• The velocity of a freely falling object increases at a constant rate.
 
• **3) Velocity does not change with time - Non-uniform motion:**
 
• If the velocity of an object does not change with time, it means the object is moving with uniform velocity.
 
• Uniform velocity implies uniform motion, not non-uniform motion.
 
• Non-uniform motion is when velocity changes with time.
 
• An object with a constant velocity has zero acceleration.
 
• Uniform motion is motion in a straight line with constant speed.
 
• **4) Velocity varies with time - Uniform motion:**
 
• If the velocity of an object varies with time, it means the object is undergoing non-uniform motion.
 
• Uniform motion implies that the velocity remains constant.
 
• Uniform motion has constant velocity, and zero acceleration.
 
• If velocity varies, then acceleration is present.
 
• Non-uniform motion can have varying degrees of acceleration.
